The table gives, for each degree k, the nodes above k, the edges among them, and phi(k): 0.6, 0.833, and 1.0 at k = 2." width="100%"} The rich-club coefficient `φ(k)` measures the connectivity among high-degree nodes (the 'rich club' of the network). For each degree `k`, it computes the ratio of actual edges to potential edges among nodes with degree greater than `k`: `\\phi(k) = \\frac{2E_k}{N_k(N_k - 1)}` where: - `N_k` is the number of nodes with degree > k - `E_k` is the number of edges among those nodes A rich-club coefficient close to `1` indicates that high-degree nodes tend to be connected to each other, forming a 'rich club'. Values less than expected in random graphs suggest the hubs avoid connecting to each other. Because high-degree nodes are likely to meet even by chance, the raw `φ(k)` is easiest to read against a baseline. With `normalized=True`, each `φ(k)` is divided by the average `φ(k)` of `n_samples=` random graphs that keep every node's degree: each is a copy of the graph rewired by `Q=` times as many double-edge swaps as there are edges (`a-b, c-d` becomes `a-d, c-b`), never creating self-loops or parallel edges. A normalized value above `1` means the hubs are more tightly knit than their degrees alone would explain. Directed graphs keep each node's in- and out-degree. Normalizing needs a graph with at least four nodes and two edges, and no self-loops or parallel edges. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, divide each coefficient by that of degree-preserving random graphs (see above). Defaults to `False`, which returns the raw coefficients, quickly and deterministically. NetworkX's `rich_club_coefficient()` defaults to `normalized=True`, so pass it explicitly when porting code. [Q]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How many swaps per edge to attempt to make while randomizing each reference graph. Defaults to `100`, as in NetworkX. Up to `10 * Q` times as many swaps as edges are tried; if the graph is too constrained to reach the target, the rewiring keeps the swaps it managed rather than raising an error (NetworkX raises in that case). Only used when `normalized=True`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random rewiring, so that normalized results are reproducible. If `None` (default), the rewiring is seeded from system entropy. Only used when `normalized=True`. [n_samples]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of random graphs whose coefficients are averaged before dividing. Defaults to `1`. More samples give a steadier baseline and make a zero average, which would leave the ratio undefined, less likely. Must be at least `1` when `normalized=True`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping degree `k` to rich-club coefficient `φ(k)` (or to the normalized ratio when `normalized=True`). Only degrees for which at least `2` nodes have degree > `k` are included (otherwise the coefficient is undefined). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : With `normalized=True`: if the graph has self-loops or parallel edges, has fewer than four nodes or two edges, if `n_samples=` is below `1` or `Q=` is negative, or if the random graphs average a coefficient of zero at some degree (try a larger `n_samples=`). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} For each degree threshold $k$, the coefficient is $\phi(k) = \dfrac{2\, E_{>k}}{N_{>k}(N_{>k} - 1)}$, the observed density among nodes with degree strictly above $k$. Self-loops and edge weights are excluded; for directed graphs the threshold applies to total degree. A rising $\phi(k)$ curve suggests that hubs preferentially wire to other hubs, the classic rich-club effect first characterized by Zhou and Mondragón (2004). The raw values returned here are *unnormalized*, which matters because $\phi(k)$ trivially approaches $1$ near the top of the degree spectrum: so few nodes remain to divide by. To decide whether a real rich-club signal is present, `normalized=True` compares against $\phi_{\mathrm{rand}}(k)$ computed on degree-preserving randomizations of the graph and returns the ratio $\phi(k)/\phi_{\mathrm{rand}}(k)$ (Colizza et al., 2006). Each random graph comes from its own stretch of one seeded random stream, so the `n_samples=` graphs differ from one another even with a fixed `seed=`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Analyze hub connectivity in a network: ::: {#03ab1839 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a network with clear hub structure graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["hub1", "hub2", "hub3", "spoke1", "spoke2", "spoke3"]) .add_edges( [ # Connect hubs to each other (rich club) ("hub1", "hub2"), ("hub2", "hub3"), ("hub3", "hub1"), # Connect spokes to hubs ("hub1", "spoke1"), ("hub2", "spoke2"), ("hub3", "spoke3"), ] ) ) rc = graph.rich_club_coefficient() # Returns rich club coefficients dict # Higher values at larger k indicate hubs prefer connecting to each other rc ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {0: 0.4, 2: 1.0, 1: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: Compare with random network: ::: {#d631b833 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Scale-free networks often show rich-club phenomenon ba_graph = ec.Graph().add_pa_graph(100, 3, seed=7) rc = ba_graph.rich_club_coefficient() # Check if high-degree nodes are more interconnected than expected # Filter coefficients > 0.5 to see strong rich-club effect {k: phi for k, phi in sorted(rc.items()) if phi > 0.5} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {13: 0.5238095238095238, 14: 0.7333333333333333, 15: 0.8, 16: 0.8, 17: 0.8, 18: 0.8333333333333334, 19: 1.0, 20: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: The raw values climb toward `1` at the top of the degree range partly because so few nodes are left there. Normalizing against degree-preserving random graphs shows how much of that is a genuine preference of hubs for one another (values near `1` mean no more than chance): ::: {#425b2e1b .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} rc_norm = ba_graph.rich_club_coefficient(normalized=True, Q=10, seed=23, n_samples=5) {k: round(phi, 2) for k, phi in sorted(rc_norm.items())[-6:]} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {15: 1.38, 16: 1.38, 17: 1.38, 18: 1.32, 19: 1.67, 20: 2.5} ``` ::: :::
